subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it be a shared execution policy rather than a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source inspection shows the requested mode is absent, but choosing when channel identity may skip approval prompts changes a security boundary and config surface that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep Existing Approval Model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts must use existing exec/elevated policy with host approvals configured permissively.

options.title: Add Telegram-Only Shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a narrower patch but higher policy-drift risk from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security policy and config-surface decision, with Telegram and approval owners involved after the direction is set.
